MAJOR: Contradictory re-review policy: `config/design-contract.json` + `review_ledger.problems(max=1)` require an HIL `MATERIAL_CHANGE` for a second diff review, while `REVIEW-TRIAGE-POLICY.md`/`WORK-EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md` describe a free one-pass delta re-review; `gate2_completion_check` enforces the stricter rule, so following the documented triage flow blocks delivery.

`architect_review_check` drops delta-mode evidence (`is_full_evidence_path`) *before* the freshness fallback, so a candidate whose only current evidence is a `--since` re-review has no accepted evidence; AC-1's delta loop cannot close the fast gate.

`_ingest` sets `review_scope` from the presence of `base`, not from whether prior reviews exist: a first full review invoked with `--since <merge-base>` is recorded as `delta` and fails Gate 2 with `DELTA_ONLY_REVIEW`.

New blocking gates depend on artifacts absent from this diff: `scripts/dev/delivery_completeness_check.py` (added to `ci-cd-gates.json` and `precheck`) and `.github/workflows/pf-gates.yml` (required by `pf_process_check`) — either every precheck/CI run fails closed, or the dependency is unverified.

Design/implementation divergence: the invariant and scope promise risk-tier gate selection (`T0/T1` no gates, `T2/T3` full, `config/risk-tiers.json`, `item.risk_tier`), but only BIIS tiers `1/2/3` + `item.tier` exist and no tier→gate mapping is implemented anywhere.

No rollout/backfill for `review_ledger`: `REVIEW_LEDGER_MISSING` is enforced from the cutover date for every contract-enforced item, while `--backfill` is a manual command not wired into precheck/CI or the item's rollout plan — all in-flight items will fail Gate 1/2 on the cutover date.

AC-3 (encoding gate incl. working-tree/untracked) is unproven: the diff adds only `test_changed_covers_committed_worktree_and_untracked`, which monkeypatches `encoding_check.changed`; `scripts/dev/encoding_check.py` is neither changed nor in the declared affected files, so the gate behavior that AC-3 requires is asserted, not demonstrated.
MINOR: `current_sha()` and `controls()` are duplicated verbatim in `control_gate.py` and `control_runner.py`; two copies of the evidence-binding hash will drift and break Gate 2 evidence matching.

`current_sha()` hashes only `git diff --binary HEAD` (tracked, non-untracked); PASS evidence stays valid after new untracked files are added, contradicting this item's own untracked-coverage requirement.
`control_runner` records `phase` values `pre/post/fix` but `control_gate` never reads `phase`, so pre-implementation evidence satisfies the `implementation` phase check.

Tier detection is substring matching over title/objective/in_scope (`"auth"` matches "author/authority"; `"ui/"`,`"ops/"` rarely match), producing systematic false tier-3/2 escalation and boilerplate `tier_reasons`.
Scope discipline is prompt-only: the prompt asks for `[OUT_OF_SCOPE]` prefixes but no parser filters them, so a prefixed BLOCKER/MAJOR still blocks in `gate_view`.
`design_contract_check` treats any `://` string as existing evidence and any `go test`/`pytest` string as an existing test, so coverage/evidence requirements are trivially bypassable.
`test-framework/tests/conftest.py` sets `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` autouse for the entire suite — an unrelated global test-env override that hides DB-path regressions.

Prompt sizing is unbounded: diff cap raised to 500k chars and the full design body + prior context + guardrails are appended with no token budget, so large items overflow context or silently truncate.

`precheck.worktree_fingerprint` covers HEAD/heads/index but not worktree content or non-head refs; any gate that legitimately touches the index/HEAD aborts the whole run, and content mutations are missed.
`config/*.yml` added to the store-registry exclusion list: future YAML configs silently escape registry coverage.
`docs/BIIS-LEARNING.md` commits a machine-specific path (`C:\Users\ADMIN\...\pf-probe`) and probe artifacts, contradicting the framework-neutral claims.
Three independent cutover dates (`2026-10-26`, `2026-10-27`, `2026-11-02`) across `design-pack.json`, `design-contract.json`, `biis-tiers.json` with no single migration record.
`allowed_check_prefixes` is duplicated in `control-matrix.json` and `guideline-compliance.json` with different values (`bash `/`sh ` present in one only).
NIT: `pf_process_check` constructs the workflow name as `"pf-gates" + ".yml"`; obfuscated literals in a validator hurt readability.
`biis_completeness_check.problems` re-reads and re-parses the config inside a per-dimension loop.
Four different "SHA" notions (`review_sha`, `head_sha`, `diff_sha`, `current_sha`) are used interchangeably in code and docs; name them distinctly.
`self_review_check` excludes `scripts/dev/` and tests, so its token ban is near-vacuous for this repository.
`_ingest` returns exit code `2` after the evidence file is already written and renamed, leaving partial state with an undocumented code.
`docs/README.md`/`gen_docs_index.py` mark new docs "Implemented 100%" though some describe unimplemented enforcement (risk tiers, runbooks).
SUMMARY: The core delta/design-pack/encoding machinery is reasonable and mostly well-tested, but the diff is far larger than the item's stated single capability: ~20 new gate scripts, 10+ configs, CI rewiring, and a governance rewrite in one item — which violates the framework's own "one capability per item, split on >2 majors" rule.

Highest risk: the review-loop logic is internally inconsistent (`review_scope` derivation, delta-evidence filtering, and the budget rule in three places), so AC-1's re-review path will either fail closed incorrectly or require an exception every time.
Second risk: fail-closed gates now depend on files not present in the diff, and a hard ledger cutover with no backfill will block all in-flight items on the cutover date.
AC-3 is asserted rather than demonstrated; AC-2 is met by `design_pack.check/render` plus the new contract checks.
